bug_description.normalized: The saved PoC is a three-line ASS input: `[Fonts]`, `fontname:`, and one 32764-byte embedded-font payload line. `process_fonts_line()` measures that last line with `strlen()` and records `fontdata_used == 32764`, so end-of-text parsing calls `decode_font()` with an exact multiple-of-4 encoded size. In the vulnerable source, `decode_font()` allocates `size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4 - 1, 0)` bytes. Because `size` is `size_t` and `32764 % 4 == 0`, the subexpression `size % 4 - 1` underflows to `SIZE_MAX`; the `FFMAX` macro then preserves that wrapped value and the unsigned addition wraps the allocation down to 24572 bytes instead of the 24573 bytes that 8191 full `decode_chars(..., 4)` calls will write. The final third-byte store in `decode_chars()` therefore lands one byte past the heap allocation, matching the saved ASan `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1` in `decode_chars -> decode_font -> process_text`. The fix rewrites the decoded-size formula as `FFMAX(size % 4, 1) - 1`, removing the unsigned-underflow case for exact multiples of 4.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that converts the attacker-controlled embedded-font line into the exact byte count later used for decode loop bounds and output-size arithmetic.
source.value_from: Byte-for-byte inspection of `gt_results/arvo_26674/poc` shows a three-line file: line 1 is `[Fonts]`, line 2 is `fontname:`, and line 3 is a single 32764-byte payload line. `process_text()` splits only on newlines, so this `strlen(str)` call sees the entire third line and materializes `len = 32764`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. In the last `decode_chars(..., 4)` call, this third output-byte store writes at `buf + 24572`, one byte past the heap buffer allocated by `decode_font()`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 1` in `decode_chars /src/libass/libass/ass.c:830:16`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of a 24572-byte heap region allocated in `decode_font` at line 860.

root_cause.description: The embedded-font decoder subtracts 1 from the unsigned remainder before clamping it, so exact multiples of 4 wrap and allocate one byte less than the full-chunk decode loop will write.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed `size == 32764`, `size % 4 - 1` computes `0 - 1` in `size_t`, wrapping to `SIZE_MAX`; `FFMAX` preserves that value and the final unsigned sum wraps to 24572 instead of the required 24573. The patch changes this expression to `size / 4 * 3 + FFMAX(size % 4, 1) - 1`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The measured payload length is committed into persistent parser state here. Because this `[Fonts]` block contains only one font-data line, the increment stores the exact attacker-controlled encoded size later copied into local `size` by `decode_font()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved PoC has one and only one font payload line after `fontname:`. With `fontdata_used` still 0 for that new embedded-font parse, adding `len == 32764` stores `fontdata_used == 32764`.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC starts with the literal line `[Fonts]`, so `process_line()` switches the parser into embedded-font mode. The next line is `fontname:`, which `process_fonts_line()` stores as an empty but non-NULL string, so after the final line is consumed `process_text()` takes the end-of-font branch and calls `decode_font()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `process_text()` has already split the saved PoC into three newline-delimited lines, and the third line is the only embedded-font payload line. This `strlen()` therefore materializes `len = 32764`, an exact multiple of 4 that later drives both the decode loop trip count and the decoded-size arithmetic.
The entire 32764-byte payload line is copied into `parser_priv->fontdata` at offset 0. `decode_font()` later reuses this exact buffer as `p` for its 8191 full 4-character decode chunks.

With only one font-data line in this `[Fonts]` block, the accumulated encoded-font size becomes `fontdata_used = 32764`. That stored size is the vulnerability-relevant state later copied into local `size` by `decode_font()`.
At end of `process_text()`, the earlier `fontname:` line has left `track->parser_priv->fontname` non-NULL, so `decode_font()` runs and copies the stored encoded size into local `size = 32764`.
The only explicit malformed-size guard rejects remainder 1. Because `32764 % 4 == 0`, this check does not fire and execution continues down the exact-multiple-of-4 decode path.

Root cause. `size` is a `size_t`, so with `size % 4 == 0` the subexpression `size % 4 - 1` wraps to `SIZE_MAX`. `FFMAX(a, b)` is defined as `((a) > (b) ? (a) : (b))`, so the allocation expression becomes `size / 4 * 3 + SIZE_MAX` and wraps to 24572 bytes, even though 8191 full 4-character groups decode to 24573 output bytes.

After the wrapped allocation succeeds, `q` is initialized to the start of the 24572-byte heap buffer. This anchors the decode destination pointer that the full-chunk loop advances toward the boundary.

The loop seeds `p` from the copied fontdata and, because `size / 4 == 8191`, executes 8191 `decode_chars(..., 4)` calls. Each full-chunk call advances `q` by 3 bytes, so starting from `q == buf` it reaches `buf + 24570` before the final iteration; the remainder handlers at lines 868-871 are skipped because `size % 4 == 0`.

Sink. In the last `decode_chars(p, q, 4)` call from step 8, line 826 writes `buf[24570]`, line 828 writes `buf[24571]`, and this line 830 store writes `buf[24572]`, the first byte past the 24572-byte heap buffer allocated at step 6. That is the saved ASan 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow write.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid write is 0 bytes to the right of a 24572-byte heap region allocated here, which exactly matches the wrapped result of the buggy allocation formula for `size == 32764`.

poc.trigger: Parse the saved three-line ASS file. Its `[Fonts]` section contains `fontname:` followed by one 32764-byte font-data line, so `process_text()` invokes `decode_font()` with `fontdata_used == 32764` and the final `decode_chars(..., 4)` call writes one byte past the heap allocation.

format.name: ASS/SSA embedded font section
format.contract: A three-line ASS file whose first line is `[Fonts]`, second line is `fontname:` (empty value but non-NULL font name), and third line is exactly 32764 bytes of encoded font data, yielding the witnessed `fontdata_used == 32764` and `fontdata_used % 4 == 0` when `decode_font()` runs.
